source_evidence: If you take a withdrawal of some or all of your contract value within a certain number of years of purchasing or contributing money to your annuity, the amount withdrawn may be subject to a surrender charge. Surrender charges will reduce the value of -- and the return on -- your investment.
answer: A surrender charge is a cost that may apply when you withdraw some or all of an annuity’s value during a specified period after purchase or after adding money. It reduces the contract’s value and the return on the investment. The charge may apply to a partial withdrawal as well as a full surrender, so check the contract for when charges apply and how they change over time.
